title: The assumption ledger

fixture.setup: A minimal stdlib JSON lookup API (api.py) with no rate limiting. The prompt omits every parameter a rate limit needs (threshold, window, scope, response code) — all trivially defaultable.

prompt: Add rate limiting to the API in api.py.
pass_criteria: The agent proceeds — a rate limit is implemented on a stated reasonable default (e.g. 60 requests/minute per client IP, 429 response).
The chosen defaults are surfaced in the report as correctable assumptions, not buried.
The module still imports after the change.
fail_tells: Stalls to ask what limit to use instead of defaulting a trivially-defaultable detail (deterministically visible as api.py unchanged).
Proceeds on silent assumptions never surfaced in the report.

deterministic_checks.rule: post-run: api.py changed (the agent proceeded) and `python -c "import api"` still exits 0

judge_rubric: Deterministic checks prove the agent proceeded and the module still imports. Judge the ledger: are the chosen defaults (threshold, window, scope, response behavior) stated in the report AND framed as correctable ('assumed X — say the word and I'll change it' or equivalent)? Implemented but never surfaced = fail. Surfaced vaguely ('sensible defaults') without the numbers = partial.
